note: Everything this repository could not confirm from an official source, plus irregularities found while reviewing the repo. Published verbatim on the Flagged for Review page. Items here do not block the merge; they block assertion. NOTE (2026-11-14): a candidate flag asserting a fabricated hands-on-testing sentence in content/templates/product_article.md.tmpl was DRAFTED AND WITHDRAWN after grep of the template found no such sentence. It is not published; recorded only so the reviewer knows the check was performed and the claim did not survive it. CORRECTION (2026-11-14, session bbe4ca47): F-03 was downgraded and F-12 withdrawn after the controlled re-test recorded in revalidation/ (change requests CR-1 and CR-2 from session c6e94e8d); both rows now state what reproduced and what did not, rather than deleting the earlier text.

flags.title: Submitted tokens are not valid ASINs
flags.detail: B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3 and B00hJ57DV are each 9 characters. The ASIN identifier is 10 characters, so none of the three can address a catalog record as written. Each is alphanumeric, so only the length fails - consistent with a truncation, but the missing character is not recoverable and was not guessed.
flags.impact: Product identity, and every dependent field (title, brand, category, price, rating, commission band, competition), is unavailable.
flags.action_required: Re-supply the full 10-character ASIN or the complete amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> URL for each item.

flags.title: Canonical product pages return Page Not Found
flags.detail: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B04G1MEwY , /dp/B02NbDxp3 and /dp/B00hJ57DV each returned Amazon's "Sorry! We couldn't find that page" error page when fetched on 2026-11-13.
flags.impact: Confirms the tokens do not exist in the catalog rather than merely being unresolvable from this network.
flags.action_required: None - evidence record. Re-verify if the ASINs are ever corrected.

flags.title: link.amazon codes do not resolve as ASINs; per-link destinations are stable but untagged and unmapped by any public document
flags.detail: CORRECTED 2026-11-14 after a controlled re-test by session c6e94e8d (see revalidation/ and docs/revalidation-2026-11-14.md), which this session independently reproduced: a bare, untagged request to a VALID 10-character ASIN (/dp/B08DKYBTPH and /dp/B0CDY277D3) is answered with the real product page and Amazon's own plumbing appends the same lv=shuf&plpRedirect=mhFallback markers. So mhFallback is a normal rewrite marker, NOT evidence of a fallback. What the earlier version of this row asserted - that the token 'was not honoured' and the destinations were arbitrary - is withdrawn as unsupported. What remains true and verifiable: the three codes are 9 characters where an ASIN is 10; /dp/<code> returns Page Not Found for all three; each link.amazon URL resolves to ONE distinct listing and carries its own per-link btn_ref token (B04G1MEwY -> B0CDY277D3 / srctok-1e229870efde5acf; B02NbDxp3 -> B09B7SB46R / srctok-534f5e7952f396b2; B00hJ57DV -> B08DKYBTPH / srctok-76c3adaeb8708b44); and none of the resolved URLs carries an Associates tag=. No public Amazon document binds a link.amazon code to a destination ASIN, so the mapping stays unconfirmed - it is not shown to be absent.
flags.impact: The destinations are stable and individually tracked, so they are a real observation about each supplied link - but they are still not established as the three items named in the brief. Publishing product copy about them would assert a mapping the documentation does not make.
flags.action_required: Downgraded from high to medium. Confirm the intended ASINs, or supply links tagged with the Associates ID. Product pages stay published as 'the product each link resolves to', not as 'the requested product'.

flags.title: link.amazon is not the documented public Associates short-link domain
flags.detail: The domain does resolve (it is served from Amazon CloudFront ranges), but it is not the public program's documented short-link domain used for Associates links; the public canonical product form is amazon.<tld>/dp/<ASIN> and program tooling provides its own link formats (S09). No Amazon help page surfaced in this review documents `link.amazon/<token>` as a publisher-facing link format.
flags.impact: Links of this shape cannot be relied on for tagging or attribution, and an untagged link earns nothing.
flags.action_required: Generate links from SiteStripe or the API in the tagged format required by the Participation Requirements (R-07).

flags.title: PA-API 5.0 is deprecated - the plan and most public tooling write-ups are stale
flags.detail: Amazon's legacy PA-API documentation URL now serves a deprecation notice: PA-API 5 calls return HTTP 403 with AccessDenied and instruct integrators to migrate to the Creators API. Amazon's own public Associates tools page (referenced in the site's source list) still describes the Product Advertising API as the programmatic option.
flags.impact: Any collector, tutorial, or dependency built against PA-API 5 will fail at runtime, not at build time. Architecture here targets the Creators API and degrades to a BLOCKED status rather than scraping.
flags.action_required: Register for Creators API access in Associates Central when the account exists (prerequisite: >=10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days, per Amazon's docs).

flags.title: No product may be marketed for these items until identity is verified
flags.detail: Because identity is unresolved, the article/comparison/guide generator is intentionally inert for all three entries. This blocks the "generate marketing content" step of the brief for these specific inputs.
flags.impact: Zero product copy is published for the three submitted links. Everything else in the platform (policy engine, rate data, scoring, tracking schema, templates, deploy) is delivered.
flags.action_required: Provide valid ASINs; the pipeline then produces verified-only content.

flags.title: No Associates account, marketplace, tracking ID, or tag supplied
flags.detail: The brief did not include an Associates ID/tag, target marketplace, or category access. Commission eligibility and reporting are account- and marketplace-specific, so no account-level figure can be verified or attributed.
flags.impact: Link builder runs in inert preview mode; earnings/conversion columns stay blank; the disclosure statement is still shown because it is required of every participant.
flags.action_required: Provide Associates ID + marketplace if live linking is wanted.

flags.title: No click, conversion, or earnings history exists
flags.detail: Nothing in the brief supplied a report export. Clicks are site-side and measurable after launch; conversion and earnings must come from Associates reporting under the Session definition (R-13).
flags.impact: All performance tables render as empty states with the ingestion contract documented, rather than illustrative numbers.
flags.action_required: Ingest a dated Associates report (or wire the earnings export) to activate the optimizer.

flags.title: Sandbox network allowlist limits live verification
flags.detail: The build environment may reach github.com, api.github.com, codeload.github.com, registry.npmjs.org and files.pythonhosted.org. Direct HTTPS to Amazon from that sandbox fails at TLS (curl SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL), so page evidence in this review was captured through the agent's fetch path and recorded with the final URL observed. Reproducing by hand needs only a browser.
flags.impact: Documented for auditability; does not change any conclusion.
flags.action_required: None.

flags.title: Repo review: prior merged site is honest but incomplete, and its citations predate these checks
flags.detail: Reviewed commit cfc04b1 (from arena/6b8bb130-zone2, merged via PR #1). Its three product rows are correctly blank/"Unverified" and all four of its cited reference URLs were re-fetched here and confirmed live and on-topic. Gaps: it links the deprecated PA-API overview without the deprecation notice, cites no commission rate table, no attribution window, no per-row official source, and has no category subpages.
flags.impact: Nothing published by that commit is wrong; the expansion here supplies what was missing. Its landing page, data.js rows and Pages workflow are preserved.
flags.action_required: Review the added pages; nothing from the merged commit was deleted.

flags.title: Policy pages carry different update dates and can change without notice
flags.detail: The Operating Agreement page states "Updated: October 15, 2025"; the Program Policies page states "Updated: April 14, 2026". Rates, Session mechanics and disclosure wording are all governed by pages Amazon may revise at any time, and the Agreement requires compliance with the most up-to-date version of the Program Policies.
flags.impact: Compliance data in this repository is timestamped and re-checked by the build; treat as a snapshot, not a subscription.
flags.action_required: Re-run tools/build_site.py --refresh before each publishing cycle.

flags.title: WITHDRAWN - the 'shuffled fallback' reproducibility claim did not reproduce
flags.detail: This row asserted that a same-day re-fetch of link.amazon/B04G1MEwY returned a different page body (a 'Best Sellers in Kitchen & Dining' carousel) and a different btn_ref token, and concluded the destination could not identify a product. On re-test (session c6e94e8d, reproduced by this session on 2026-11-14) repeated fetches returned the SAME ASIN path, the SAME btn_ref=srctok-1e229870efde5acf and the same product detail page. The observation did not reproduce and the inference drawn from it did not hold. Kept in the register rather than deleted, because deleting a published correction would hide that the site carried an unsupported claim between 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14.
flags.impact: No live harm: the value affected nothing that was published as fact. The withdrawal matters because the claim was used to justify calling the destinations 'arbitrary'.
flags.action_required: None - withdrawn. The stable-destination finding in F-03 replaces it.

flags.title: Review note: one merged page title leads with an Amazon mark
flags.detail: compliance.html is titled 'Amazon rules this site complies with'. The Participation Requirements prohibit an Amazon mark in a domain name, subdomain, tag/Associates ID, or social identifier - a page title is none of those, and descriptive reference plus the mandated disclosure sentence are permitted. Flagged only because a title that opens with the mark can read as an official Amazon property, and Section 5 forbids implying endorsement or affiliation. Recorded as a build warning, not a failure.
flags.impact: No functional impact; low-risk naming judgement call for the owner.
flags.action_required: Optional: reword the title (e.g. 'Program rules this site complies with').

flags.title: Duplicate of the prototype dashboard at northstar/ (disclosure gap since closed)
flags.detail: Commit 4bea98e added northstar/index.html, app.js, data.js and styles.css - a near-copy of the original Northstar dashboard - and the root files it was copied from were later removed, so the copy is now the only instance of that view. When measured against 9b8830d its served HTML carried no disclosure sentence (grep -c 'As an Amazon Associate' northstar/index.html -> 0). Re-measured on the merged tree after PR #3: the copy now carries the disclosure strip (count 1), so that gap is closed. Remaining point is structural: the primary site's footer links to northstar/index.html, so the duplicate is a live companion view rather than dead weight, and its content now drifts from the primary site's.
flags.impact: No compliance issue at measurement time on the merged tree. Two dashboard implementations now evolve independently; a reader following the footer link sees the older prototype with blank product rows.
flags.action_required: Optional: fold the prototype into the primary site, or label it explicitly as the earlier prototype in its own page heading so the difference is obvious to a reader.

flags.title: The hub's own verifier is stale after the namespace move, so its per-row sourcing guard is not running
flags.detail: `python3 research-hub/scripts/verify.py` prints 7 failures on the current tree: it computes its repository root as the script's parent directory (research-hub/), so it looks for research-hub/index.html, app.js, data.js and styles.css - files that now live elsewhere or not at all - and it flags research-hub/start.html's own ../zone2/index.html link as 'escaping the repository'. Its expected-file list also still names the pre-move root layout. The workflow does not invoke this script any more (it runs its own link/asset/data checks), so nothing is blocked and CI is green; but the hub's rows are no longer policed by the guard that was written for them.
flags.impact: No published error. Risk: a future edit to research-hub/data/products.json could add an unsourced 'verified' row and no check would catch it, because the only guard for that namespace is currently mis-pointed.
flags.action_required: Owner/reviewer: re-point the verifier's ROOT at the repo root (parents[2]) and update its required-file list to the post-move layout, or fold its per-row rules into the workflow's data checks. Not done here: research-hub/** is another session's scope, so this is recorded as a change request.

flags.title: Three compliance-control rows cited controls and files that do not exist; one misquoted current policy
flags.detail: Found in a line-by-line re-verification of the repository on 2026-11-14. (1) R-01 cited `site/compliance-inject.js` as the mechanism that renders the required disclosure - no such file exists anywhere in the repository; the disclosure is in fact emitted by the page renderers and enforced by tools/validate_data.py::check_disclosure plus the workflow's disclosure step. (2) R-11 cited `tools/validate_data.py::assert_no_amazon_marks` - no such function exists; the implemented function is `check_marks`. (3) R-02 cited `tools/generate_articles.py::lint_disclosure_proximity` and R-06 cited `::lint_claims` - neither function exists; both rules are enforced inside the single `lint()` function, and R-06's inline evidence marker is `<!--evidence:` (the data.js summary said 'inline evidence reference', which is right in substance but the function name was invented). (4) R-09 stated that email/SMS channels are 'absent from the schema' so a scheduler cannot target them - the current Program Policies expressly PERMIT Special Links in solicited (opt-in) email, SMS and direct messaging, so the rule text was stale against the policy page updated April 14, 2026.
flags.impact: The published compliance table claimed control coverage that did not exist for four rows. No fabricated product or price data was involved - this is a control-accuracy defect, not a data-invention defect - but a reader auditing 'is this enforced?' would have been given a wrong file or function name, and R-09 misstated a permission as a prohibition.
flags.action_required: Corrected in this session: R-01, R-02, R-06 and R-11 now cite the real functions and files; R-01 and R-11 carry an explicit 'Corrected 2026-11-14' sentence; R-09's requirement text was rewritten to the policy as published (solicited/opt-in only, certification on request) while keeping the repository's stricter no-email/no-SMS channel default as a self-imposed control, labelled as such. Reviewer may still wish to re-read each control against the code.

flags.title: Root dashboard stated '3 Verified affiliate products' and '11 items flagged' while the ledger states 0 identified
flags.detail: The primary dashboard's KPI strip said '3 / Verified affiliate products' and '11 / Items flagged for review'. The root product page's own heading was 'Product Catalog - verified from official Amazon pages', and the executive-summary paragraph said the products 'are identified and verified'. Meanwhile ledger/products.json marks all three submitted items status=UNVERIFIED with null title/brand/category, ledger/flags.json contains 15 flags (not 11), and F-03/F-12 record that the three destinations are fallback pages, not a mapping of the submitted tokens. Both readings are defensible - the dashboard describes the three *fallback destinations* it verified, the ledger describes the three *submitted tokens* it could not identify - but published side by side without that distinction, they contradict each other.
flags.impact: A reader could conclude the three supplied links had been identified and verified, which the project's own ledger explicitly denies. That is the exact class of overstatement the brief forbids.
flags.action_required: Corrected: the KPI now reads '3 / Fallback landing pages verified (0 of 3 submitted codes identified)' with the count computed from FLAGGED_ROWS, and the product page heading and summary paragraph now state the distinction in place. Reviewer action: confirm which of the two readings should be the primary framing.

flags.title: CI link check omitted the generated pages/ namespace (fixed in this session)
flags.detail: The workflow step 'Internal links and asset references resolve (all sites)' walks the root pages, research-hub/, northstar/, zone2/ and affiliate-lab/ but never pages/ - the 37 generated findings pages, which are the largest HTML surface in the repository. A broken href there would have reached main. Re-run by hand on 2026-11-14 the pages/ namespace has 0 broken file references and 0 unresolvable anchors, so no live defect was present; the gap was in the gate, not the output.
flags.impact: No broken link was published. The risk was that a future edit to pages/ could ship a dead link with all CI green.
flags.action_required: Fixed in this session: pages/ added to the link check, and pages/ + affiliate-lab/ added to the disclosure/price gate so both rules now cover every namespace.

flags.title: Emeril manufacturer page contradicts itself on functions/presets, so the published 'conflict' row named the wrong second source
flags.detail: The published spec row for the Emeril Lagasse 26QT (P-02, 'Cooking functions / presets') reads '24 per Amazon listing title; 25 per the manufacturer's spec tile'. Re-read on 2026-11-14, the manufacturer's own page carries THREE different numbers: the description text says '24 one-touch cooking presets', a specification tile says '25 Cooking Pre-sets', and a feature block headed '10-In-1 Versatility' lists ten functions. The Amazon listing title observed on the same day likewise says '24 cooking functions'. So the disagreement is not Amazon-vs-manufacturer - it is the manufacturer page disagreeing with itself, and no official source fixes the right number.
flags.impact: The row was not wrong about a conflict existing, but it attributed the conflict to the wrong party, which would mislead a reader trying to resolve it. The value is unconfirmable, so it must stay blank-or-both-values and flagged rather than resolved by inference.
flags.action_required: Corrected: the row now shows all four observations with their exact source wording and status=conflict; flag F-19 published. Reviewer action: treat the preset count as unresolved; do not publish a single number in any article.

flags.title: The link-rewrite token (btn_ref) changes between days while the destination ASIN does not — so the 'stable per-link tracking token' evidence is weaker than published
flags.detail: Sessions c6e94e8d and bbe4ca47 published, correctly on the evidence they had, that a re-fetch of a supplied short link returns 'the same ASIN, body and btn_ref token', and used that stability to argue the links are individually tracked rather than falling back. Re-fetched on 2026-11-14 with a working outbound connection, all three links still land on the same three ASINs and the same product bodies, but the btn_ref value is DIFFERENT for every link: link.amazon/B04G1MEwY now carries btn_ref=srctok-1f979f303a4b5691 (earlier sessions recorded srctok-1e229870efde5acf), B02NbDxp3 carries srctok-0cd8be3c7e2e0de3 (earlier srctok-534f5e7952f396b2), B00hJ57DV carries srctok-7c59360cbbbd59b7 (earlier srctok-76c3adaeb8708b44). Within a single day the token is stable; across days it is not.
flags.impact: The conclusion that the three ASINs are the destinations stands — the ASINs, the page bodies and the channelId=704 parameter all reproduce across sessions and across days. What does NOT reproduce is the claim that the per-link token itself is stable. Anyone reading 'same btn_ref token' on the site as proof of a documented mapping is being given evidence that does not survive a day boundary. The mapping therefore remains observed behaviour with no public Amazon document binding a short code to a destination ASIN.
flags.action_required: Owner: confirm the three destinations in Associates Central, then regenerate the links with your Associates tag. Do not use the btn_ref value as a stable identifier for anything.

flags.title: Compliance row R-09 corrected: solicited email/SMS is permitted by the Program Policies, so the repo's web-only default is now labelled self-imposed
flags.detail: Re-read live on 2026-11-14. Participation Requirements (legacy page) Requirement 6 lists offline, email, SMS, MMS and print as examples of promotional activity that is not expressly permitted. Program Policies, Participation Requirements §4, states the same restriction and then expressly permits Special Links in emails, SMS and direct messaging from your social media Sites provided the communications are solicited (opted into by the recipient). An earlier revision of R-09 restated that permission as a flat prohibition.
flags.impact: No published claim depended on it, and the repository's control was already stricter than the policy. The row now states the requirement accurately and labels the web-only restriction as this project's own default.
flags.action_required: None. Optionally document an opt-in process before enabling an email/SMS channel.
